headline: PLS.AX slides nearly 4% as lithium pessimism deepens, while the ASX 200 dropped 0.7% today and the RBA rate outlook continues to dominate headlines.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara dropped 3.75% today as lithium stocks broadly sold off across the ASX mining sector. Investor sentiment on lithium remains divided — analysts are debating whether the cycle has bottomed or has further to fall. PLS is now down 12.3% from your entry price.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF slipped 1.74% today, dragged lower by weakness in chip stocks. Broadcom tumbled ~13% in its last US session after its AI chip revenue guidance disappointed markets, which knocked the broader AI/semiconductor space and flowed through to GXAI here on the ASX.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets dipped 0.94% today. No single catalyst — general risk-off tone on the ASX, combined with a slightly stronger Aussie dollar (which reduces the AUD value of foreign assets), weighed on this one.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL slid 0.8% today as oil prices softened. OPEC cut its oil demand forecast for 2026, and crude (WTI) fell to around $92/barrel in the last US session. Lower expected demand = lower energy company revenues = lower ETF price.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft nudged up 0.17% in its last US session — a quiet, positive day. The stock continues to benefit from its strong AI positioning. Q1 earnings showed Microsoft outperforming most automation software peers, keeping sentiment steady.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two rose 0.39% in its last US session. There's some fun buzz around GTA 6 — the Rockstar boss actually became a playable character in a promotional move — keeping the game in the news cycle ahead of its anticipated release.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG edged up 0.12% today — a small, steady gain. As a diversified high-growth fund it largely tracked the mixed market conditions, with US exposure (via VTS-type holdings inside the fund) providing a slight tailwind.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS rose 0.31% today, reflecting last night's positive S&P 500 session (up 0.41%). The broad US market held up well despite some tech weakness, and that flowed through to VTS's ASX close today.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: No live price data available for GOOG today — the previous close was $355.68 USD. Keep an eye on it tonight when US markets open; Broadcom's AI chip guidance miss last session rattled some AI names, but Google separately announced an $85B expansion bet which was well received.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium pain continues — hold or trim?
watch_today.detail: Pilbara dropped another 3.75% today and is now 12.3% below your cost price. Kalkine describes the stock as a 'battleground' with investors split on whether lithium has bottomed. There's no clear positive catalyst right now, but selling locks in the loss. Hold unless your conviction on the lithium recovery thesis has changed.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Broadcom shock hits AI ETF — hold
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 1.74% today after Broadcom dropped ~13% in the last US session when its AI chip guidance disappointed. The ETF is now 5.15% below your cost. The broader AI story remains intact (Google's $85B expansion, continued model launches), so this looks like a sector wobble rather than a trend change. Hold and watch tonight's US session.

watch_today.title: Broadcom fallout: watch US markets tonight
watch_today.detail: Broadcom's 13% tumble last US session on softer-than-expected AI chip guidance rattled the semiconductor sector — the SOXX chip index fell 2.1%. This affects GXAI.AX directly and could also weigh on GOOG and MSFT tonight when US markets open around 11:30pm AEST. Worth checking in later.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Steady as she goes — hold
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is up 0.17% in its last session and continues to be the market's favourite AI play. Microsoft's AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman says his team is 'more concerned' about Anthropic than Google or Meta as competition. Q1 earnings showed MSFT outperforming automation software peers. Still down 3.4% from your entry — no rush to do anything here.

watch_today.title: RBA rate cut expectations building — good for your Aussie holdings
watch_today.detail: CBA has formally forecast RBA interest rate cuts, and the RBA itself flagged an early housing slowdown as rate rises bite. Markets are now pricing in cuts sooner than previously expected. Lower rates typically boost ASX valuations and reduce mortgage stress — a tailwind for your VDHG.AX, VTS.AX and any Australian equity exposure inside those funds.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil demand outlook weakens — hold
watch_today.detail: OPEC cut its 2026 oil demand forecast, and crude (WTI) is sitting around $92/barrel. FUEL slipped 0.8% today but is still 2.86% above your cost price — a small winner in your portfolio. The energy sector faces headwinds if demand forecasts keep being revised down, but you're still in profit. Hold for now.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a soft day today, falling 0.7% to close at 8,625. The broader mood was cautious — lithium, gold and mining stocks dragged the local market lower. Over in the US last night, it was a mixed picture: the S&P 500 rose a solid 0.41% to 7,584, but the NASDAQ barely moved (down 0.09%), weighed down by Broadcom's big drop after its AI chip guidance disappointed. Gold hit a fresh high near $4,489 USD/oz, oil softened to around $92/barrel, and the Aussie dollar is holding steady at about 71.4 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Soft close today — mining and lithium stocks led the losses

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — solid gain, broad market held up well

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Last night — basically flat, Broadcom's 13% drop offset gains elsewhere

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: OPEC cut demand forecasts for 2026, oil drifting lower

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Continuing its strong run — near record highs

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Steady — RBA cut expectations keeping a lid on any big AUD surge

ai.summary: A big week for AI governance — tech giants including Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic signed a joint letter warning about AI-enabled bioweapons, while US lawmakers are moving to block individual states from regulating AI. There's also fresh competition data showing GPT-5.5 dominating real-world tests.

stories.title: Tech giants warn AI + synthetic DNA = bioweapons risk
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and other major AI players have co-signed an open letter sounding the alarm about a specific risk: synthetic DNA and RNA sequences that could be repurposed to make biological weapons are already accessible online — and AI can now teach people how to use them. The letter is essentially calling on governments to urgently regulate access to this combination of tools before a 'shock event' forces their hand. This is the industry admitting publicly that AI poses risks they can't self-manage alone.

stories.title: US House drafts bill to strip states of AI regulation power
stories.why_it_matters: US House lawmakers have released a draft bill that would prevent individual US states from passing their own AI regulations — all AI rules would have to come from the federal level. This is a big deal for the industry: instead of navigating 50 different state rulebooks, companies like Google, Microsoft and OpenAI would only have to deal with one (potentially more industry-friendly) federal framework. Critics argue it guts consumer protections that states like California have been building.

stories.title: Microsoft's AI chief says Anthropic is their biggest worry — not Google
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft's AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman says his team watches Anthropic (maker of the Claude models) more closely than Google, Meta or OpenAI when it comes to competitive threats. This is a candid admission about how fast Anthropic is moving. For MSFT holders, it's worth knowing that Microsoft is clearly taking the competition seriously — which tends to drive continued investment and innovation rather than complacency.

stories.title: GPT-5.5 dominates $1,500 real-world hacking test; Gemini refused to participate
stories.why_it_matters: In a real-world cybersecurity test costing $1,500, OpenAI's GPT-5.5 dominated the field — apparently the best at identifying and exploiting vulnerabilities. More striking: Google's Gemini reportedly refused to even attempt the test. This kind of benchmark matters because it shows practical capability gaps between models, and raises fresh questions about AI being used for offensive hacking. It's also a reminder that the AI race is intensifying fast.

stories.title: Broadcom's AI chip miss dents sector confidence
stories.why_it_matters: Broadcom fell 13% in the last US session after its AI chip revenue guidance came in below what Wall Street was hoping for. The broader chip ETF (SOXX) fell 2.1% as a result. This is the tension in the AI trade right now: the software and model side keeps impressing, but some of the hardware infrastructure companies are struggling to meet sky-high expectations. Google separately announced an $85 billion expansion bet which was well received — showing the AI investment cycle isn't over, just more selective.

sport.summary: Manly won last night's NRL opener for Round 14, beating the Rabbitohs 28-14. There's some controversy over a 'sticky spray' ruling. AFL is in its bye round and the Jordan Dawson health story is dominating footy headlines. Wimbledon chatter is also starting to heat up.

stories.title: Sea Eagles 28 def. Rabbitohs 14 — but win comes with controversy
stories.why_it_matters: Manly beat the Rabbitohs 28-14 at 4 Pines Park last night to kick off Round 14. The result continues the Sea Eagles' strong form behind the Kieran Foran resurgence. Souths were stung by a controversial 'sticky spray' no-call ruling — the referee later gave a surprise explanation for not penalising it. The win came at a cost for Manly though, with injury concerns to be monitored.

stories.title: Broncos halfback succession plan hits a twist — Suncorp derby on Saturday
stories.why_it_matters: There's a major contract twist brewing at the Broncos around their halfback succession plan, with Fox Sports reporting shock heat on key stars ahead of the Broncos vs Titans Suncorp Stadium derby on Saturday night. The details are under wraps but it's the kind of internal drama that can unsettle a squad mid-season. Keep an eye on team lists dropping tomorrow.

stories.title: AFL world rallies around Adelaide captain Jordan Dawson
stories.why_it_matters: Adelaide Crows captain Jordan Dawson is going through something serious off the field and has been described as 'superhuman' by the AFL world rallying around him. The 7NEWS report says emotions poured out as teammates, opponents and fans united in support. No further details on the nature of the situation were available at time of publishing, but the outpouring of support suggests it's significant.

stories.title: Greg Rusedski flags concern about Djokovic ahead of Wimbledon
stories.why_it_matters: Former British No.1 Greg Rusedski says he has 'one concern' about Novak Djokovic's readiness for Wimbledon, which is now just weeks away. No specific detail from the article text was available, but the broader Wimbledon build-up is underway with Serena Williams also reportedly confirmed to make a doubles comeback alongside her partner ahead of the tournament.
